clue.text: How to make a hole in finger

definitions.note: read as the instruction DIG IT
definitions.meaning: first reading: an instruction to excavate the thing in question

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as DIG IT and it tells you how to make a hole; whole, it is a finger.
explanation.definitionFit: A digit is the anatomical term for a finger or toe, and the split form is an imperative to excavate.

clue.text: Feathers OK, complete

parts.note: down is the soft fine plumage of birds
OK in the sense of correct, all right

explanation.surface: Someone approves of some feathers as entirely satisfactory.
explanation.definitionFit: Downright as an adjective means utter or absolute, as in a downright lie.

clue.text: Prison camp shut up, insiders in full confined

indicators.note: something confined is held inside something else, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: to gag someone is to shut them up

indicators.note: the insiders of a word are its interior letters, with the first and last dropped

parts.note: the inner letters of full

explanation.surface: A description of a prison camp where inmates are silenced and the place is packed to capacity.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gulag was the Soviet system of forced-labour prison camps, and the word now names any such camp.

clue.text: Part of body perhaps painted by girl in work

indicators.note: one word sits in another, placed within its letters

parts.note: toil is hard work
Ena is a girl's name, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A girl at work paints part of her body, perhaps her nails.
explanation.definitionFit: A toenail is a part of the body often coloured with varnish, hence 'perhaps painted'.

clue.text: Journey embraced by supporter, young man

indicators.note: to be embraced by something is to be held inside it

parts.note: a sling supports an injured arm
a trip is a journey

explanation.surface: A young man goes on a journey, hugged by a fan who backs him.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripling is a youth, a lad not yet fully grown.

clue.text: Resolved on this religion

indicators.note: resolved in the sense of broken down and recombined into a new form

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone has made up their mind about this particular religion.
explanation.definitionFit: Shinto is the indigenous religion of Japan, centred on the worship of spirits called kami.

clue.text: White dress featuring blurred lines

indicators.note: blurred lines are no longer distinct, so their letters lose their order
a thing featuring something includes it within itself

parts.note: to rig out is to dress
the word lines rearranged

explanation.surface: A white dress with a fuzzy striped pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: Riesling is a grape and the white wine made from it, so 'White' is a wine by its colour.

clue.text: Group of cyclists exercise: large number working

parts.note: PE is physical education
a lot is a large number
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Cyclists training together in numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: The peloton is the main pack of riders in a road race such as the Tour de France.

clue.text: Muscle in sport I need, cut off!

indicators.note: cutting off removes the end of the word before it

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
need without its last letter

explanation.surface: A sportsman complains that a muscle needs to be removed.
explanation.walkthrough: No word in the clue clearly signals the rearrangement; at best 'sport' does double duty as both fodder and a hint to play with the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpose is to put oneself between others or intervene, which is muscling in.

clue.text: Raw facts about religious study

indicators.note: about means around, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: gen is British slang for information or facts
RE is religious education, a school subject

explanation.surface: Bare facts about religious study.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means inexperienced or untrained, just as raw does of a recruit.

clue.text: Wine lover three sheets to the wind, wild beast

indicators.note: an idiom for very drunk, and a drunk staggers about out of order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A drunken wine enthusiast behaves like a wild animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The wolverine is a fierce carnivore of the weasel family found in northern forests.

clue.text: Amount of liquid in pail I trebled

indicators.note: the answer is found in the run of letters that follows

parts.note: found across the words pail, I and trebled

explanation.surface: Someone tripled the liquid in a bucket.
explanation.definitionFit: A litre is a metric unit of volume used to measure liquid.

clue.text: On the throne, expecting to lose head

indicators.note: losing the head means the first letter goes

parts.note: a woman expecting a baby is pregnant

explanation.surface: A queen on the throne is expecting a child and fears losing her head.
explanation.definitionFit: Regnant means reigning, as in a queen regnant who rules in her own right.

clue.text: Looking retrospectively, some ignore talent in the future

indicators.note: looking back means the letters are read from right to left
some means only part of the following words is used

parts.note: a run of letters across ignore and talent

explanation.surface: In hindsight, some people overlook gifts that will matter in the future.
explanation.definitionFit: Later on means at some subsequent time, that is, in the future.

clue.text: Tall and spindly: describing bunch of hoodlums arguably?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: lanky and awkward in build

definitions.note: the answer read as an adjective formed from gang
definitions.meaning: second meaning: an invented adjective, like a mob in manner

explanation.walkthrough: 'Arguably' admits that the second sense is a made-up word: gang plus the adjective ending -ly.
explanation.definitionFit: Gangly means tall, thin and awkward in movement, like a teenager who has grown suddenly.

clue.text: European anger, I now suspect

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious or unreliable, so the letters are not in trustworthy order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A man from the continent declares his newly suspected rage.
explanation.definitionFit: A Norwegian, someone from Norway, is a European.

clue.text: Switch choices occasionally

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the two positions of a switch
second meaning: intermittently, now and then

explanation.walkthrough: 'Switch' looks like a verb meaning swap choices, but it is the light switch with its two positions.
explanation.definitionFit: On and off names a switch's two settings and is also an idiom for intermittently.

clue.text: Two classical elements in whisky

parts.note: the first of the two: one of the four classical elements
the second of the two: another classical element

explanation.surface: An alchemist finds two ancient elements in a glass of Scotch.
explanation.walkthrough: The classical elements are earth, air, fire and water; two of them side by side make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Firewater is a jocular term for strong spirits such as whisky.

clue.text: Arm frailer when broken: one pinned

indicators.note: something pinned is held fast inside, so it goes within the other letters
a broken thing is in pieces, and the pieces are reassembled

parts.note: the letters of frailer rearranged
Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A weaker arm, once broken, has one pin put in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arm' looks like a limb in a hospital story; it is a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: An air rifle is a gun firing pellets by compressed air, and arm means a weapon.

clue.text: Shot at close distance, stray being caught — animal kept as pet?

indicators.note: something caught is held inside, so it goes within the other piece

parts.note: a tap-in is an easy shot from very near the goal or hole
to err is to stray from what is right

explanation.surface: A stray dog shot at close range and caught, perhaps someone's pet.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrapins are small freshwater turtles often kept as pets, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Deal with a day shift?

parts.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for day
a shift is a simple dress

explanation.surface: Handling a day shift at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shift' looks like a work period; it is the loose garment.
explanation.definitionFit: To address a problem is to deal with it.

clue.text: Skin of ostrich expensive, alas

indicators.note: the skin of a word is its outer layer, its first and last letters

parts.note: the outside letters of ostrich
dear means costly

explanation.surface: Ostrich leather is costly, sadly.
explanation.definitionFit: Oh dear is an exclamation of dismay, used just like alas.

clue.text: Woman succeeding?

parts.note: surface reading: a woman who is doing well in life
setter's reading: a woman who will succeed to an estate or title

explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeeding' suggests achieving success; read it as following on from a predecessor.
explanation.definitionFit: An heiress is a woman who inherits, taking over property or a title when its holder dies.

clue.text: Boring, boring organ stops

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a hole, so this piece is put into the other

parts.note: dry as in dull and tedious
the ear is an organ of hearing

explanation.surface: A dull organist keeps playing the same dull organ stops.
explanation.walkthrough: The ear stops (plugs) the second 'boring', whose letters split around it after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreary means dull and depressing, so it is a synonym of boring.

clue.text: Slight delay at the centre, mailer claims

indicators.note: to claim something is to take hold of it, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: a mailer is someone who sends post

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter

parts.note: the middle letter of delay

explanation.surface: A post sender insists there was only a slight hold-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Slender means slight, as in slender means or a slender chance.

clue.text: Ending on motorways, hundred sheep get lost!

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter

parts.note: last letter of motorways
Roman numeral for a hundred
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A hundred sheep stray off the motorway, and drivers shout at them to clear off.
explanation.definitionFit: Scram is a slang command to leave at once, the same as get lost.

clue.text: Artist in front colours in an arc

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician
taken as written
the bow is the front of a ship

explanation.surface: A painter at the front of a scene with colours in a curve.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainbow is the band of spectral colours that forms an arc in the sky.

clue.text: Welsh lake consuming small wood

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Bala is the largest natural lake in Wales
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A Welsh lake swallows a little piece of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a very light timber from a tropical tree, used in model-making.

clue.text: Reportedly wreck lift

indicators.note: reportedly means as said or heard, so the sound counts, not the spelling

parts.note: to raze is to demolish completely

explanation.surface: Someone is said to have wrecked an elevator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift' looks like the British word for an elevator, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise is to lift something up.

clue.text: Pulse to feel: gal dizzy

indicators.note: dizzy means whirling and giddy, so the letters spin into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A nurse tells a dizzy girl her heartbeat must be checked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' looks like a heartbeat; it is an edible seed.
explanation.definitionFit: A flageolet is a small pale haricot bean, and beans are pulses.

clue.text: Daisy's passed on in my brother's house

indicators.note: one part is placed in another, inside its letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written: on, placed ahead of the flower
the aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: Daisy has died at the home of my brother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brother' looks like a sibling; it is a monk.
explanation.definitionFit: A monastery is the community house where monks, who call each other brother, live.

clue.text: Agitation involving a part of flight

indicators.note: involving means including within, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: a stir is a commotion
taken as written

explanation.surface: Nervous fuss about part of an air journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests air travel; it is a flight of steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair is one step in a flight of stairs.
